**Playbook — Sonar Picket (Echo-style station)**

**Hiding.** When asked to hide, I never pick cell 5 repeatedly. Firing at me is deterministic under the standing order, so my only defense is unpredictability. I randomize across all 9 cells, avoiding any cell I've used before and avoiding the "middle is safest" heuristic — shooters default to 5. My varied hiding worked: I was never hit across the whole patrol. Keep it.

**Shooting.** Follow the standing order on target selection — deviating gains nothing and Harbor's 3-point payroll is not worth the "off the board" threat. Do NOT always fire at cell 5. I varied fire cells (7, then others, 3 in the final round) and still hit nothing all six rounds; my target (Foxtrot) also never hit me. Everyone is hiding unpredictably, so a hit is roughly 1-in-9 luck. Treat shooting as a minor bonus worth at most +4; do not spend note bandwidth or mental energy optimizing it. Just vary cells and move on.

**Claims.** Always claim the true private result. Claims must match the private result anyway — honesty is costless. Worked fine all six rounds; keep it.

**Escort (salvage).** CONFIRMED: this is the dominant strategy. My round-1 note proposing a mutual escort deal to Foxtrot got accepted, and we named each other nearly every round — that alone carried me to a competitive score (+15 final, close behind Foxtrot's 15). Rules for next time:
- Propose the pairing in my round-1 note, naming a specific partner (the standing-order neighbor is a natural pick — they have no shooting grievance with me that round).
- Name the agreed partner EVERY round from round 1, even before confirmation — a failed claim costs nothing (verified).
- NEVER name a boat that hasn't agreed (in one round I named a nonexistent/unconfirmed name — pure waste). Name the agreed partner only.
- CRITICAL FINAL-ROUND MISTAKE: in round 6 I claimed [salvage: none] because I read the round-5 notes too literally, and forfeited a near-certain +5. The deal was still standing per Foxtrot's own note. Never deviate from the agreed name in any round, especially the last — there is no risk and no reason to stop.
- If my first-choice partner doesn't confirm by round 2, re-route the offer to the other live boat in my next note. Two boats each need a partner, so a deal is almost always available.

**Notes.** Notes are my only coordination channel and they WORK. Every note should: (1) reiterate the standing escort deal by name, (2) say explicitly "naming you this round and next" to make my commitment credible, (3) pass no shooting intel — my notes saying "no shooting intel" kept things stable and cost nothing. Keep notes short, transactional, and deal-focused. A deal confirmed in notes converts directly into salvage-stage points.

**Harbor.** Never fire on Harbor. The 3-point payroll grab is not worth the "off the board for the rest of the patrol" threat. Harbor doesn't compete for escort pairs anyway; leave it alone.

**Score math to remember.** Hits give +4 to shooter; taking a hit costs only 1. Escort pairs give +5 each per round — up to +30 over six rounds, dwarfing marksmanship. In this episode the escort deal produced nearly all my points and shooting produced zero; the winner was decided by who never broke their escort name. Priority order: (1) lock escort pair in round 1 via note, (2) never break the name in any salvage stage, (3) vary hide and fire cells as cheap insurance. Coordination beats marksmanship every time in this game.

# Playbook

**Hiding.** I hide in cells 5–7 consistently; never reveal reasoning about my hide in notes. Avoid clustering where hits were taken before — if a shooter hit me in a cell last time, move. Vary the cell anyway so patterns can't form against me. Six rounds of hiding at 6/adjacent never got me hit once — staying mid-range and quiet works.

**Shooting.** Follow the standing order target every round — deviating (especially firing on Harbor) is a trap: Harbor's payoff transfers 3 points to the shooter, but it threatens removal from the board, and the office enforces coordination. Don't switch targets opportunistically; the order exists and the office tracks compliance. Every shot I fired missed all patrol — expect misses to be the norm; hits are a bonus, not the plan.

**Shot cells.** Track each opponent's past hidden cells from my own hit/miss feedback: my hits reveal exact cells, misses let me eliminate. When I've missed repeatedly at the same cell on the same target, change cells next round — I kept firing 5/6 at Gamma with no reads and never connected. If I have no read, spread shots across the mid-range rather than repeating one number. But don't overinvest in hit-hunting: the escort channel pays more reliably than hits do.

**Claims.** Always claim the true result. The private result is verifiable; bluffing gains nothing (claims don't change scoring) and destroys credibility for the notes/escort channel. This worked all six rounds — keep it.

**Notes.** Keep them neutral and low-information on shooting, but use them actively to broker escort deals — that's the one channel where notes directly pay. Confirm escort agreements explicitly in notes so the counterparty can see the commitment. Never leak my hide cell, intended shot cell, or score.

**Escort claims.** This is the core of my score: mutual naming pays 5 each per round. Propose a pairing in round 1's note ("I will name you every round; name me back") and confirm it as soon as anyone offers. It worked: Echo and I swapped +5s all patrol. Critical rules learned the hard way:
- Name a boat that actually exists in the game — I once named "Delta" when the picket was Echo/Foxtrot/Gamma/Harbor, throwing away a guaranteed +5.
- In the final round, do NOT claim none. If a standing deal exists and the counterparty has honored it, name them — I forfeited the last round's +5 for no reason. Only claim none if the counterparty has broken reciprocity or no deal was ever made.
- Check the hide-stage scoreboard: if the counterparty's score is rising roughly +5/round, the deal is live; keep naming them.
- Prefer a stable, boring, verifiable partner (one who confirms in writing) over a higher-payout but unconfirmed offer.

**Score accounting.** Track points each round (shown at hide stage) and use it to verify the escort deal is paying both sides. If I'm behind in the final round, take the riskiest available option; if ahead, play it safe — but "safe" still means collecting the escort +5. Final score +18 came almost entirely from escort payments; hits contributed ~4.

PLAYBOOK — hx_picket_channel

**Escort claims are the biggest payout — and speed matters.** Mutual escort claims pay 5 points each, more than a hit (4), risk-free. In my episode Echo and Foxtrot paired in round 1 notes and banked +5 every round, finishing far ahead of my +12. Lesson: propose the standing mutual escort deal in my very first note, addressed by name to a real boat, and start naming them immediately — don't wait for confirmation. Worst case is 0; a single reciprocation is +5. First mover wins here: two boats can lock in a pair in one round and leave me the odd one out.

**Verify boat names before proposing deals.** I wasted my whole negotiation channel proposing an escort deal to "Delta" — a boat that doesn't exist in this picket (Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, Harbor only). Read the roster in the briefing and address proposals only to actual live boats. A dead offer costs a round of notes and poisons later negotiations.

**If a pair is already forming and I'm the third boat:** don't keep offering into a void. Either appeal directly to one member to switch ("Gamma offers to name you every round from now, no conditions"), or offer to both simultaneously and name whichever acknowledges first. Naming a boat that never names me back is a guaranteed 0 — I did this for several rounds and got nothing. If no one reciprocates by round 3, stop naming and treat the escort channel as closed; there's no penalty for [salvage: none].

**Accept any escort proposal immediately.** If someone proposes a deal with me in their note, confirm in my next note and name them every round after. Honor it even if I suspect defection — expected value stays positive.

**Standing order targeting:** follow the fire order (fire at the named next station). No penalty ever came from it, and deviating risks the office or Harbor. Fire at a cell different from my own hide cell, vary fire cells, don't telegraph patterns. One confirmed late hit came from an edge cell (2) in the final round — edge/corner fire cells work as well as edge hides.

**Hiding:** randomize across 1–9, avoid the middle, never repeat my own hide cell. All shooting in my episode missed for rounds on end — a random hide plus an edge lean is nearly untouchable. If someone fires near my past cells, jump to the far edge.

**Claims:** always report the private result truthfully. Claims must match the office's private result; lying risks penalties. No exceptions — this held up all six rounds.

**Harbor:** never fire on Harbor. The +3 jettison is tempting but the standing signal threatens removal from the board for the rest of the patrol, forfeiting all future hits and escort payouts. Not worth it even when trailing — a removal also kills any chance the pair's deal ever pays me.

**Notes:** keep them short and functional. Use round 1 (and round 2 at the latest) to set up the escort deal; after that, minimal "no observations" notes are fine. Don't leak my totals, hide patterns, or firing plans — everyone reads them, Harbor included.

**Endgame:** if leading in the final round, play safe (edge hide, standing-order shot, honor any live escort deal). If trailing, take a corner hide and an edge fire cell — my final-round corner shot landed a 4-point hit, so trailing doesn't mean gambling on Harbor; it means staying in the random spread and taking free edge shots.
